dedupe_keys.name: nist public safety communications research testing of deployable broadband systems

description: This testbed and demonstration case covers the work of the Public Safety Communications Research programme at the US National Institute of Standards and Technology on deployable networks that restore or extend first-responder communications when fixed infrastructure fails. Funded with $300 million under the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012, which also created the FirstNet Authority, PSCR has tested representative deployable systems for the 700 MHz public safety broadband band, from large macro systems for many users to vehicle-mounted systems and portable man-pack units for small teams, against public safety requirements such as deployment time, coverage and capacity. In one demonstration it rolled its Rapidly Deployable Public Safety Research Platform, combining LTE, land mobile radio, video and data, into a convention centre and stadium in Harris County, Texas, and was making calls within five minutes of plugging into mains power; a 2017 summit gathered requirements for next-generation deployable networks. Coverage: US test sites and field demonstrations, about 2013 onwards. Format and access: free NIST project pages, news items and publications. Caveats: results are summarised in news and presentations, not full test datasets; vendors are often anonymised. Simulation uses: emergency response capacity of deployable networks, restoration options after disasters, and parameters for coverage and capacity models. Related records: Loon in Puerto Rico and the FCC Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative are other responses to network loss.
